title: A Novel Framework for Human-like Reinforcement Learning: ARDNS-P with Piagetian Stages
content: Human reinforcement learning (RL) integrates probabilistic reward estimation, multi-timescale memory, and adaptive learning strategies that evolve with cognitive development—features often absent in traditional RL models like Q-learning and Deep Q-Networks (DQNs). This paper introduces the Adaptive Reward-Driven Neural Simulator with Piagetian Developmental Stages (ARDNS-P), a novel framework combining neuroscience-inspired mechanisms with Jean Piaget’s theory of cognitive development. ARDNS-P employs a Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) for reward prediction, a dual-memory system for short- and long-term contextualization, a variance-modulated plasticity rule, and a developmental progression inspired by Piaget’s stages (sensorimotor, preoperational, concrete operational, and formal operational). We evaluate ARDNS-P against a DQN baseline in a dynamic 10x10 grid-world environment. ARDNS-P achieves a 79.8% goal-reaching success rate (2394/3000 episodes) compared to DQN’s 25.5% (764/3000), with greater efficiency in steps to goal (14.4 vs. 39.02) and slightly higher cumulative rewards in the last 200 episodes (0.8499 vs. 0.8378). ARDNS-P demonstrates strong potential for human-like learning in cognitive AI, robotics, and neuroscience-inspired systems, though further optimization is needed to reduce reward variability.
